title: Life Cycles of Living Things
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Life Cycles of Living Things Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Plants and animals have life cycles: seeds germinate, grow, flower and make seeds; animals are born or hatch, grow, reproduce and die. Life cycles can be compared. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 2: Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Living Things): plant life cycles, germination, animal life cycles, comparing life cycles and metamorphosis. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every living thing has a life cycle.
key_sub: A seed needs water, warmth and air to germinate.
body_html:
How to think about it

A flowering plant's life cycle: seed → seedling → adult plant → flower → fruit and seeds. A seed germinates when it has water, warmth and air.

Animal life cycles: mammals are born live and grow; birds and most reptiles hatch from eggs; insects such as butterflies and amphibians such as frogs undergo metamorphosis. All living things reproduce so that the species continues.

Example

What does a seed need to germinate?

Not light

Answer: water, air and warmth

Example

Stages of a frog?

Four stages

Answer: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult

Common mistakes

  • Thinking seeds need light to germinate.
  • Thinking all young animals look like their parents.
  • Thinking plants do not have a life cycle.

faq.a: Flowers make seeds so that new plants can grow.

faq.q: Why do frogs lay many eggs?
faq.a: Many eggs and tadpoles are eaten, so laying many helps some survive.

items.q: How are burdock seeds spread?
c: Their hooks stick to animal fur and clothing.
items.e: Burrs hitch a ride.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the adult plant with flowers?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the young plant?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: What is pollination?
c: moving pollen from one flower to another
items.e: Bees, butterflies and wind carry pollen.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, which comes first: new seeds forming inside a fruit or seed dispersal?
c: Neither is part of the life cycle.
They happen at the same time.
new seeds forming inside a fruit
items.e: Seed → germination → seedling → adult plant → flowers → pollination → seeds in a fruit → dispersal.

items.q: Which part of a flower becomes the fruit?
c: the ovary (the bottom of the pistil)
items.e: Fruit protects the seeds.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes after the young plant?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

It protects the inside of the seed.
It grows downwards and takes in water.
It stores food for the young plant.
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: What is germination?

items.q: Which plant has a life cycle that can last hundreds of years?

items.q: What happens to a plant at the end of its life cycle?

items.e: Life cycles repeat.

items.q: Why do many flowers have bright petals and a sweet smell?
c: to attract insects that carry pollen
items.e: Insects help pollinate.

items.q: Does a seed need light to start growing (germinate)?
c: No. A seed has food stored inside, so it can start growing without light.
Only if it is a big seed.
Yes, a seed cannot start without light.
items.e: Seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate. They use food stored inside them until their leaves grow.

items.q: How do many berry seeds get spread?
c: Birds eat the berries and drop the seeds far away.
items.e: Animals help plants spread.

items.q: Does a seed need water to germinate?
c: Yes. A seed needs water, air and warmth to germinate.
No. A seed needs only soil.
No. A seed needs only light.
Only seeds planted in pots need it.
items.e: Seeds germinate when they have water, air and a suitable temperature.

items.q: Does the young (caterpillar) of a butterfly look like its parent?
c: Yes, but it has more legs.
No, it looks very different from the adult.
Yes, it is a smaller copy of the adult.
items.e: The young changes a lot as it grows: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: In the life cycle of a butterfly, which stage comes after the caterpillar (larva)?
items.e: The life cycle of a butterfly is: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a mosquito in the correct order?
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a butterfly?
items.e: Butterfly: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: Does the young (nymph) of a grasshopper look like its parent?
c: Yes, it looks like a smaller adult.
Only after it becomes a pupa.
items.e: The nymph looks like the adult but is smaller and has no wings.

items.q: In the life cycle of a chicken, which stage comes just before the adult chicken?
